Every realized 2x2 update is aI+bJ, hence has norm multiplier |R|^2. Averaging the four sign patterns under their unique p-coupling gives x^3 Q_{s,p}(x)/9216. Independence across steps proves m^k for every deterministic input. The discriminant of Q_{s,0} and exact monotonicity in p classify all boundaries, including s=1,p=0. Extracted standalone exact-rational checker passed 1523 assertions; finite tests support rather than replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating full article defines the algorithm and describes consistency and plotted deterministic perturbation stability, but no formula for this two-error binary coupling mean-square phase. The closest published stochastic TDRK work analyzes the distinct two-stage method with shared noise; a published antithetic Heun result uses first-derivative component sampling. Actual full-text comparisons found neither direct equivalence nor a stronger theorem implying the sharp s>1/3 and p<(3s-1)/(10s) classification. Historical priority is qualified.

value.rationale: The two curvature evaluations of a newly proposed fourth-order, second-derivative rule provide a natural uncertainty-coupling question not answered by deterministic stability charts. An exact, complete and sharp phase diagram shows a qualitatively surprising transition: unbiased anti-correlated errors create squared-energy contraction where the error-free, independent-noise and shared-noise steps do not, with unique optimal coupling at every step. This exposes limits of interpreting perturbation-order and norm stability separately. Its scientific value is a boundary classification, not a claim of improved physical accuracy or feasible hardware benefit at very large error amplitudes.
